dataset_family: ADNI (single-shell 3T diffusion subset; 472 CN, 136 EMCI, 60 LMCI after motion exclusion)
method_family: Single-shell free-water DTI (f-index, fw-FA, fw-AX, fw-RD), voxelwise TFCE plus whole-WM ROI, with ANTs Atropos tissue volumetry (WM, GM, CSF fractions)
what_it_shows: Bergamino, McElvogue and Stokes 2025, NeuroSci 6:8 (Barrow Neurological Institute, ADNI data). Whole-white-matter ROI: the free-water fraction (f-index) separates CN from EMCI (t = -6.822) and from LMCI (t = -4.128), while whole-WM fw-FA, fw-AX and fw-RD separate no pair (fw-FA F = 0.101, p = 0.904). Tissue volumetry: WM volume separates CN from LMCI and EMCI from LMCI but not CN from EMCI (Dunn Z = 0.54, p = 1.00). GM volume and CSF volume separate CN from BOTH MCI groups (GM CN-EMCI Z = 4.35, p < 0.001; CSF CN-EMCI Z = -3.92, p < 0.001). Voxelwise, both the f-index and fw-FA have significant clusters for every pair.
why: Partly: only one narrow contrast fits. For CN versus EMCI, in essentially the same participants (the volumetric analysis dropped 3 CN and 1 EMCI who lacked T1), whole-WM free-water fraction separates the groups where whole-WM volume does not. That is a WM-diffusion versus WM-macrostructure contrast at matched spatial scale, against a non-impaired comparator. Four points limit it. (1) The static measures do not fail as a class. GM volume and CSF volume separate the same CN-EMCI contrast, and for CN versus LMCI every measure type separates. (2) The diffusion metric that succeeds is the free-water (extracellular fluid) fraction. The authors themselves tie free water to CSF increase from neuronal loss, and CSF volume, a static index, separated the same groups. So the 'loaded' measure may track the same fluid compartment the static measure already captures. The tissue-microstructure metric (whole-WM fw-FA) failed at the ROI level. (3) The authors never contrast measure types. Their own summary is that 'Volumetric analyses revealed reduced white and gray matter volumes and increased CSF volumes in the MCI groups'. The dissociation has to be assembled by the reader from Tables 7 and 8, so it is not an author-reported within-study head-to-head. (4) The paper's emphasised contrast is EMCI versus LMCI, where MMSE fails and fw-FA clusters succeed. That comparison has no non-impaired comparator, the same ground on which P-661 was judged partly and P-753/P-781/P-804 were rejected. Other limits: single-shell fw-DTI, which the authors name as the main limitation; multi-scanner ADNI data with ComBat harmonisation; the ROC analysis is computed inside significant clusters, which is circular. Dataset family ADNI: an all-ADNI exception would have to be declared if other ADNI supporters were added. No overlap with any current supporter (all single-centre, non-ADNI) or with the other candidates. Not a preprint (peer-reviewed MDPI article).

quotes.quote: Table 7 shows the ROI analysis conducted for all fw-DTI metrics within the entire white matter. Significant group differences were identified in the f-index metric (CN vs. EMCI: t = -6.822, p < 0.001; CN vs. LMCI: t = -4.128, p < 0.001).

For white matter, volume reductions were identified in the LMCI group, with significant differences between the CN and LMCI groups and between EMCI and LMCI. Regarding graygrey matter, significant reductions were observed in both the EMCI and LMCI groups compared to the CN group, with the MCI groups exhibiting decreased gray matter volumes. Lastly, CSF volumes were significantly increased in both the EMCI and LMCI groups compared to the CN group.

The f-index was higher in EMCI and LMCI groups, while fw-FA was lower compared to the CN groups. Volumetric analyses revealed reduced white and gray matter volumes and increased CSF volumes in the MCI groups.
For instance, AD is characterized by neuronal loss, which leads to increased cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) and fw across the brain.
There are some limitations to this study. The main limitation of the study is related to the single-shell dMRI acquisition.
